name: Skills & Checks
summary: Eighteen skills, two of them yours. Everything else you may still attempt — you simply do it without the bonus.

sections.heading: What a check is
paragraphs: When the outcome of something you try is genuinely in doubt, the DM calls for an ability check: roll d20, add the ability's modifier, and add your proficiency bonus if you are trained in the skill they named. Beat the DM's number and it works.
The skill decides which ABILITY you use, and nothing else. Athletics is Strength, Perception is Wisdom, Deception is Charisma — the skill is the label on the situation, the ability is the number.

sections.heading: The eighteen, by the ability each uses
list: DEXTERITY — Acrobatics, Sleight of Hand, Stealth
INTELLIGENCE — Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, Religion
WISDOM — Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Perception, Survival

sections.heading: You get two, at creation, from your class
paragraphs: Each class offers a list and you choose TWO from it. That is the only source of skill training in this system — no backgrounds hand any out and no level grants one, because your background is your character's story rather than a package of numbers (see Character Creation).

The lists are the class saying what it is: a Puppeteer reads people, a Sandow lifts and endures, an Illusionist knows things. They overlap heavily, and every skill in the game is on at least one of them, so there is nothing a member of this company can never learn.
Choose for the game you expect to play, not for the class you are reading about. Perception is the check a DM calls for more often than any other, and every class can take it.

sections.heading: Untrained is not forbidden
paragraphs: This is the half that matters most at a table, and it is worth saying plainly: you may attempt any check. Not being trained costs you the proficiency bonus, never the attempt.

So a Sandow with Wisdom +0 and no Perception training rolls a flat d20 to notice something, and sometimes notices it. Your sheet prints every skill with the number you actually roll, trained or not, and a button that rolls it — there is no such thing as a skill your sheet cannot answer for.

sections.heading: What the app does and does not do
paragraphs: The app works out the number and throws the dice where the table can see them. It does not decide the DC, it does not decide whether a skill applies, and it never tells you that you failed. This system's app is a tracker, not a referee: what the roll MEANT is the DM's, out loud, like everything else worth arguing about.
